signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme
signals.text: CHF 1W avg: +1.160% (n=6 pairs) vs AUD 1W avg: -0.715% (n=4 pairs), yielding a G10 spread of 1.874%. The extreme divergence between the strongest and weakest G10 currencies this week reflects severe risk aversion compressing high-beta commodity currencies while safe-haven flows concentrate in the Swiss franc. RBA AONIA at 4.85% vs SNB SARON at -0.04% provides a +485bp carry advantage for AUD/CHF, yet spot continues to trade under intense downward pressure as VIX sits at 26.9 (elevated volatility). The technical structure for AUD/USD shows spot at 0.6636, holding well below its SMA20/50/200 cluster and extended 3.95 ATR from its 20-day moving average in a confirmed downtrend. Meanwhile, AUD/USD retail sentiment shows 81% long, creating a vulnerability to long liquidation. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF; severe risk aversion and safe-haven demand override the carry advantage. Catalyst: Euro Area Economic Sentiment Indicator and upcoming central bank speakers. Risk: Risk sentiment abruptly normalizes, narrowing the G10 spread and triggering a sharp short-covering bounce in the laggard.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning + BEER Valuation + ECB Minutes
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0977, positioned below its SMA20 at 1.1085, SMA50 at 1.1200, and SMA200 at 1.1496 in a downtrend characterized by falling moving averages and a price sitting entirely below the 20-day average. CFTC leveraged funds net short stands at -105,891 contracts with a 52-week percentile of 2, indicating extreme positioning crowding at the lower decile of its historical range alongside a -7,287 WoW contraction. The BEER-model misvaluation z-score sits at -2.43σ, marking EUR/USD as severely cheap relative to rate differentials and risk sentiment, with spot at 1.0977 versus model fair value at 1.1119. Today's ECB published minutes confirmed that transmission is working smoothly and a hike at the current meeting was actively discussed to pre-empt second-round effects, contrasting with SOFR 3.94% vs ESTR 2.44% (+150bp carry favoring USD). Trade bias: Neutral/range EUR/USD, positioning exhaustion against extreme valuation mispricing. Catalyst: ECB meeting 17 Dec — hike probability priced by policy bias. Risk: US data outperformance keeps DXY bid above 103.73, pushing the misvaluation z-score even deeper without triggering a mean-reverting bounce.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry + VIX Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.28, holding above its SMA20 at 158.82, SMA50 at 158.18, and SMA200 at 158.85. The 25d risk reversal sits at -1.82, showing strong put skew and elevated hedging demand for downside protection as spot tests intervention thresholds near 160.00. SOFR at 3.94% vs TONA at 1.23% provides a +271bp carry premium favoring the dollar, while the USD/JPY vs VIX correlation prints at -0.097 against a 252-day norm of +0.267 (z = -2.25σ), signalling that the traditional JPY safe-haven feedback loop is disconnected while elevated VIX at 26.9 pressures risk assets. CFTC leveraged funds show JPY net short at -29,545 contracts with a 52-week percentile of 85, marking a crowded short position in the upper decile of its historical range. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported with downside options hedging against verbal intervention risks. Catalyst: Japan Tokyo CPI excl. Food and Energy y/y. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 triggers official Ministry of Finance intervention, overriding the carry differential.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Technical Reversal + OIS Carry Differential
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4230, sitting above its SMA20 at 1.4180, SMA50 at 1.4152, and SMA200 at 1.3934 in a counter-trend pullback inside a larger uptrend. The prior session recorded a bearish engulfing bar with a body measuring 1.6 times the ATR and a wide-range bar at 3.8 times the 10-bar average body, accompanied by a close below the prior 10-day closing low. SOFR at 3.94% versus CORRA at 2.56% delivers a +138bp carry advantage favoring the dollar, supported by a Fed policy rate of 4.00% against the Bank of Canada rate of 2.50%. Retail FX sentiment shows 31% long and 69% short, reflecting broad retail participation fading the broader uptrend. CFTC speculative positioning records CAD net short at -75,447 contracts with a 52-week percentile of 37, representing a moderate positioning structure without extreme crowding. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD on a counter-trend dip; carry and moving average structure favor trend resumption. Catalyst: Canada Current Account release. Risk: Continued downside follow-through breaks the SMA20 support at 1.4180 and shifts the medium-term structure bearish.
